blocks.text: Matthew 13 gathers parables about the kingdom amid changing audiences and selective explanations. Its images of sowing, fields, and fishing resonate with an unequal agrarian Roman-Palestinian economy. The formula in verse 53, “when Jesus had finished these parables,” is one of five repeated discourse-ending formulas that organize major teaching collections in Matthew. This pattern may help readers notice the chapter’s place within a larger arrangement, but it does not prove a universally accepted symbolic outline for the book.

sections.title: Reading the Parables as a Collection

blocks.text: At verse 41, language and motifs in Matthew may be compared with Zephaniah, and similar comparisons can be made with Revelation. Each proposed connection needs to be considered passage by passage: direct quotation, use of a shared tradition, and broader prophetic reuse are different claims.
